why: This is a medium-risk Python behavior change: execution reports gain an optional task-budget field and report/checkpoint resume restores and validates it before work.
not_doing: No provider call, cross-platform run, build/install, tag, Release or package-index action.
diff_walk: pocketchat/task_exec.py: write TaskBudget.to_dict() for budgeted reports, accept the additive field in the closed report parser, and before resume restore it only when its limit equals the authorized TaskBudget.
tests/test_task_exec.py: a budgeted resume of an old report without a ledger is refused before run_task.
tests/test_task_cli_resume.py: budgeted stop/resume and checkpoint resume preserve prior request rows; missing, tampered and mismatched ledgers are refused without new provider calls.
docs and CHANGELOG: replace the prior budgeted-resume refusal with the persisted-ledger contract; product slice queue marks the new delivered slice.
static_checks: Closed report schema is extended by exactly one additive optional field.
A report ledger with no spec budget is refused; a spec budget with no report ledger is refused; limit mismatch is refused.
Restored ledger rows are validated by TaskBudget.from_dict; the next reservation uses the same limit and prior requests remain.
No public CLI flag or JSON envelope field outside the execution report changes.
red_green: Before the implementation, the tests failed with missing task_budget and the old "budgeted resume is not supported" error. After the change, all focused and full tests pass on CPython 3.9.6 and 3.13.9.
gaps: Real provider usage, crash recovery, concurrent writers, build/install and cross-platform behavior remain unverified.
